findings.text: The manifest's tests: line names /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../tests/gate_review_promotion_test.py, which no longer exists, and the head gate log it cites is truncated after '..................' with no summary and no EXIT line (suite-head.log and suite-base.log are truncated the same way). 'crew check --manifest --run r-20261103T075534458753' reports exactly those three logs, so the run's gate receipt is unrunnable and the reviewed commits' result is claimed rather than recorded; repairing it means naming tests/test_a_review_runs_promotion_derives_its_own_gate.py and re-recording the two arms.

The committed fragment still states the gate arm is '4 passed' at head against '2 failed, 2 passed' at base and the suite pair '438 passed / 439 passed', but the reviewed commits' own logs/gate-base.log now records '3 failed, 15 passed' and the gate-head/suite logs carry no summary at all; the corrected prose exists only as an uncommitted working-tree edit that still contains literal SUITE_BASE and SUITE_HEAD placeholders, so a coordinator landing this record lands figures its evidence contradicts.

commits stops at 7e7251cb6a and changed_paths at line 12 never names tests/test_a_review_runs_promotion_derives_its_own_gate.py, so the record does not describe the three commits under review; the write-path audit passes only because the omitted file is also absent from changed_paths, which is the check reporting a clean result on an incomplete record.

The per-key fill lets a caller who passes only --gate-command keep their command while the derivation supplies the review record as log_path and 0 as exit_status, producing a receipt whose command and log describe different evidence; the fifth test covers both flags together and neither partial case, so this half-filled state is unguarded.
